transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, my family told me I had to come in. I just... I keep telling them that I’m the reason my friend died. I didn’t call her back when I should have, and I had these ugly thoughts sometimes. It's my fault she's gone. And now I know the Lord is punishing everybody at our church because of me. I just... I've brought all this on everyone.
Can you tell me more about what makes you think the Lord is punishing everyone at your church because of you?

It happens during the service. When the pastor says the prayers, or... when the choir sings certain lines, I just know they are really warning me. They're letting me know that God has marked me. And that the whole church is suffering because I brought this on us. I just hear it in the words they say.

When you hear the pastor or choir during service, do you ever hear voices or sounds that others don’t seem to hear, or do you feel like the words are meant only for you in a way others don’t understand?

Well, like I was just saying... I don't hear voices or sounds that aren't there. I hear the exact same singing and praying everyone else in the pews hears. But yes, I know the words are meant just for me. 

When the pastor says the prayers, or the choir sings those certain lines... I know they are warning me. The person sitting next to me might just hear a regular hymn, but I know the truth. They're warning me that God has marked me, and they're letting me know that the church is suffering because of what I brought on us. I just... I know that's what it means.

When you interpret the pastor’s prayers or the choir’s singing as warnings meant specifically for you, do you feel absolutely certain that this is true, even though others might think it’s just a regular part of the service?

Yes, I am absolutely certain. I know people might think it's just a regular prayer or a normal hymn, but... I know what it really is. When the pastor says those prayers, or the choir sings those lines, I know they are warning me. I know they are telling me that God has marked me, and that the whole church is suffering because of what I did. I don't need anyone else to believe it, because I know it's the truth.
Do you ever feel that things people say or do in other places — like on TV, in conversations, or in public — are also meant specifically for you, even if others don’t see it that way?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. It's really just at the church. I don't get any messages from the TV or from people talking at the grocery store where I work. It's just the pastor and the choir. That's where I hear it.
Do you ever feel that people at church, or others in your life, are actively working against you or treating you differently because they believe you are to blame for something bad happening?

No, I don't think anyone is actively working against me. They aren't treating me bad or anything like that. They're just... letting me know. Through the prayers and the songs. But nobody is being mean to me or trying to hurt me, if that's what you mean. They're just passing on the warning.
Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs or experiences that others might not understand, even if they weren’t related to the church or the pastor’s prayers?
No, I haven't really had anything else like that. It's just the church stuff. I go to work, I come home... nothing else strange is going on, as far as I can tell. Just the warnings on Sundays.

Have you ever had any other strong beliefs that others might not share or understand — even if they weren’t connected to the church — such as thinking that you have special powers, that someone is trying to communicate with you through hidden messages, or that something unusual is happening around you?

No, nothing like that. I don't have any special powers or anything. And like I said, there aren't any hidden messages anywhere else. Just the church. Everything else is just... normal. I go to work, I do my job at the register, I go home. That's it.
Have you ever believed something strongly that turned out not to be true, even when others tried to tell you otherwise — something that wasn’t related to the church or your feelings of guilt?

No, I haven't. I mean, I don't really get into arguments with people about things like that. I don't have any strange beliefs or anything. I just know what I know about what I've done, and what they're telling me at church. But other than that, no, nothing like what you're asking about.
Have you ever felt down or hopeless for a period of time, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy, for more than two weeks at a time?

Yes, I have. For a while now, really. I just... I don't care about the things I used to. I used to love singing in the choir, going to my knitting circle, playing bingo... even just taking walks through Patterson Park. But now, I just sit in my chair at home. None of it feels worth the effort of even getting dressed anymore. I just don't have the interest.
Have you ever had a time before this when you felt down or hopeless and lost interest in things you normally enjoy for more than two weeks?

No, I don't think so. I mean, everyone has bad days, but... nothing like this. This is the first time I've ever felt this low for this long. I've always been pretty active and involved before all this started.
Besides losing interest in things you used to enjoy, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or sleep, or have you been feeling unusually tired or worthless lately?

Well, my appetite is mostly gone. Food just tastes like cardboard to me now. I've noticed my skirts have gotten pretty loose, too, because... well, most days I really only pick at a piece of toast or have a little tea. Even when my niece makes something and puts a plate right in front of me, I just can't bring myself to eat it.
Have you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, since this started?

I'm not really sure if it's most of the day, or... or every single day. The days just sort of run together lately. I know I just sit in my chair, like I said, but I haven't really kept track of if I'm feeling hopeless that whole time. It's more that I just don't feel much of anything at all, so I can't say for sure if it's every day.
Have you felt down or sad most of the day, nearly every day, since this started?

Well, like I was just saying... I don't really know if I'd call it sad. It's just this heavy, empty feeling. I sit in my chair and the time just passes. I can't really tell you if it's every single day or most of the day because I just... I don't keep track. It's just all a blur of nothing.
